sanskrit: iyattikā śakuntikā sakā jaghāsa te viṣam | māhaṃ mṛṣi mo asau puruṣo mṛta | sa ca na marati mā vayaṃ marāma | āre asya yojanaṃ hariṣṭhā madhu tvā madhulā karat ||
english: The little śakuntikā bird has eaten your poison along with her companion. Let me not die, nor let yonder man die. He shall not die; let us not die. Far from him be its operation — the green plant shall make you sweet, the honey-sweet one shall render you honey.

sanskrit: sūrye viṣam ā sṛjāmi dṛtiṃ surāvato gṛhe | (…) ||
english: Into the sun I release the poison, into the wineskin in the house of the soma-presser. [Remainder fragmentary.]

sanskrit: triṣaptā visphuliṅgakā viṣasya puṣpakam akṣan | (…) ||
english: The thrice-seven sparkling ones have destroyed the blossom of the poison. [Remainder fragmentary.]

sanskrit: ālvantaruṭaṃ viṣaṃ vidārī karambho arasaṃ viṣam | (…) ||
english: The poison of the ālvantaruṭa plant is sapless venom; vidārī and karambha render the poison devoid of sap. [Remainder fragmentary.]

sanskrit: vār ugram arasaṃ viṣam agniś ca viśvacarṣaṇiḥ | (…) ||
english: The fierce, sapless poison of water — and Agni, the all-beholding — [neutralize it]. [Remainder fragmentary.]

sanskrit: śakuntikā me abravīd viṣapuṣpaṃ dhayantikā | (…) ||
english: The śakuntikā bird spoke to me — she who sucks the flower of the poison: [she declared it harmless]. [Remainder fragmentary.]

sanskrit: na ropayati na mādayati na viṣaṃ hanti pūruṣam | māhaṃ mṛṣi mo asau puruṣo mṛta | sa ca na marati mā vayaṃ marāma | āre asya yojanaṃ hariṣṭhā madhu tvā madhulā karat ||
english: It does not fester, it does not intoxicate, the poison does not slay the man. Let me not die, nor let yonder man die. He shall not die; let us not die. Far from him be its operation — the green plant shall make you sweet, the honey-sweet one shall render you honey.

sanskrit: navānāṃ navatīnām ity ekā ||
english: Of the ninety-nine, this is one.

sanskrit: madhumatī patye asmi jārāya madhumattarā | atho madhavyaṃ me bhaṃso madhu nipadane aham ||
english: Honey-sweet am I to my husband; yet sweeter than honey to my lover. Moreover, my vulva is honeyed; I am honey at the moment of union.

sanskrit: madhunā mā saṃ sṛjāmi māsareṇa surām iva | vāṅ ma iyaṃ madhunā saṃsṛṣṭā- -akṣyau me madhusaṃdṛśī ||
english: With honey I blend myself, as one blends fermented grain with māsara-liquor. This speech of mine is commingled with honey; my two eyes are honey-radiant in their gaze.

sanskrit: madhu dyaur madhu pṛthivī madhv indro madhu sūryaḥ | striyo yā jajñire madhu tābhyo 'haṃ madhumattarā ||
english: Honey is the sky, honey the earth, honey is Indra, honey is the sun. The women who were born honey — from all of them I am yet more honey-sweet.

sanskrit: madhumatīr oṣadhaya āpo madhumatīr uta | gāvo yā jajñire madhu tābhyo 'haṃ madhumattarā ||
english: Honey-sweet are the plants, and honey-sweet are the waters too. The cows that were born as honey — from all of them I am yet more honey-sweet.

sanskrit: madhor jāto madhugho vīrudhāṃ balavattamaḥ | tenāhaṃ sarvasmai puṃse kṛṇve nikaraṇaṃ hṛdi ||
english: Born of honey, producing honey — the most powerful among plants — with him I make an impression in the heart of every man.

sanskrit: yathāśvo bandhaneṣṭho vaḍavām abhidhāvati | evā tvam ugra oṣadhe 'muṃ kanikradatam ā naya ||
english: Just as a horse stalled in the tether rushes toward the mare, so do you, O potent herb, bring that man to me, neighing as he comes.

sanskrit: aṅgo nu mod iva śvaso aṅgo nu mod iva stanaḥ | anyā vivitsamāno anyāḥ parājighāṃsan | mām anu pra te manaś chāyā yantam ivānv ayat ||
english: How like delight his very breath, how like delight his very breast! Desiring other women, intent on surpassing them — yet your mind followed after me, as a shadow follows one who walks.

sanskrit: khananti tvā taimātāṃ dāsā arasabāhavaḥ | dāsy asi prakrīr asy utkhātam arasaṃ viṣam ||
english: The Dāsas with sapless arms dig you up on the dark side of the mother. You are a slave-woman, you are a bought-thing, you are uprooted — a sapless, impotent poison.

sanskrit: adanti tvā kakkaṭāsaḥ kuruṅgā adhi sānuṣu | pāpī jagdhaprasūr asy abhrikhāte na rūrupaḥ ||
english: The kakkaṭa crabs eat you; the kuruṅga deer eat you on the ridges. You are a wicked thing whose seeds have been eaten; dug up with a spade, you have caused no further harm.

sanskrit: ava jyām iva dhanvanaḥ śuṣmaṃ tirāmi te viṣa | pra ropīr asya pātaya sūryaḥ pūrvā ivoṣasaḥ ||
english: As the string is let down from the bow, so I unstring your virulence, O poison. Let its festering shoots fall down, as the sun makes the earlier dawns fall away.

sanskrit: sindhuḥ paścāt parihitaḥ sūryasyodayanaṃ puraḥ | tato yad antarā vanaṃ tat sarvaṃ viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: The Sindhu is spread behind, the rising-place of the sun is in front. Whatever forest lies between those two — all of that is the bane of poison.

sanskrit: madhu tvā madhukṛt kṛṇotu pituṃ tvā pitukṛt kṛṇotu | uto niṣadya pātave atho ūrdhvāya tiṣṭhate ||
english: May the honey-maker render you honey; may the food-maker render you food — both for sitting down to drink and for standing upright.

sanskrit: jaghāsa tvā lomakarṇas tan ny āsa paruṣṇiyām | tad bhaimīś cakrire srajaḥ sarvaṃ mahiṣado viṣam ||
english: Lomakarṇa devoured you and sank you into the Paruṣṇī river. The Bhaimīs fashioned garlands from that — all the poison is food for the great buffalo.

sanskrit: urvyā urukṣitas turāyā āturasya ca | bhūmyā hi jagrabha nāma viṣaṃ vārayatām iti | viṣaṃ dūṣayatād iti ||
english: By the wide, the far-striding, the swift, and by that of the afflicted — for the earth has seized its name. Let the poison be warded off, let the poison be made impotent.
